The two small hand held pads are holding up fine and I believe they will continue to hold up. The handles are firmly attached and have been withstanding heavy tugging.

The small suction cups that are meant to hold the scrubbers or the back scrubbers do not stick to my shower tile. My tiles have a slight texture to them. The suction cups keep popping off after a few hours. (Not sure of the exact amount of time it takes them to pop off. I stick them on and they are popped off around 8 hours later when I notice them.)

The texture is great and feels fantastic. I am finding that I can use either side for scrubbing if desired. The handles on the back scrubber are attached very well.

These turned yellow after two uses, despite careful rinsing with hot water. This displeases me and makes me wonder what germs are being left behind. I wash my back scrubber of any type once a week in a sink full of extra warm water and detergent. I then allow the scrubber to dry outside in the sunlight for the day. Non loofah types are run through the washer on delicate but loofahs are more delicate.

This set is a good one and the fact that it comes with a pair of each means that it can either be shared as I am doing or there can be a spare for when I wear out the first set in around 6-8 weeks. (Yes, I really do exchange my bath stuff about every two months.) Being 6'4" and 230lbs, this is a little small to use, but overall it seems to be of good quality and works as intended. The suction cups stick quite well thus far and the loofah swells quite a bit when it first gets wet, leaving an abrasive (but not too rough) cleaning texture. It's also nice to have two sets for a couple, or to set one aside for later use. This would have received 5 stars if it were a full loofah on the back scrubber, as the small area just isn't enough (about 12" long is loofah, while sides are another material).

This loofah scrubber is still too small and the length for a larger person may be very problematic, as it's very hard to get a hold of both ends at times. The smaller scrubber has been a favorite of mine and does quite well (far better than plastic loofahs) at removing dead skin in sensitive areas like the face. Both loofahs do puff up but are not uniform in size, making pressure points on the skin, while leaving some areas left untouched. This is a review of the Silicon Devices 150W High Performance Auto Power Inverter.

I have this in my SUV to allow me to use my laptop on the go. My laptop I use for travel is older and has no battery that keeps a charge. It also charges my phone but that need is rare as my phone battery keeps a nice charge.
For those who may not know what a power inverter is, it is a basic device that you can plug into a dc vehicle outlet and converts it so you can use an ac device. (DC outlet to AC outlet.) This one does have an extra bonus as it throws in two USB charging ports. The USB ports are rated 1amp and 2.1amp. (Use the higher one for your tablets and heavy power hungry devices.)
This takes in 12volts DC and puts out up to 150 watts which is plenty for normal ac devices such as laptops and portable electronics. It is only 9.6 oz and measures 4.3” x 3” x 1.7”. It is made of metal and is very durable so you can toss in your glove or utility box so it is ready to go. Cable is also nice and long so you can reach from front of the car to the middle area so others can use from all the other seats.

Cons – One thing I did notice is that the DC plug did not have a fuse in line. The description indicates this has over and under voltage protection; however, I am not clear if this is for the usb ports and or if this applies to the ac outlet as well. Other inverters typically offer fuses or a fuse if you remove the end cap on the dc plug. (On the up side, the soldering inside the dc plug was very nice and solid with nothing loose or questionable.)

Tips / Notes – Make sure your vehicle is running when you use this. This has potential to draw a good deal of power if using the upper range of 150watts and can run down your battery if the vehicle is not on allowing your alternator to prevent battery drainage.

Summary – This works as described and is very small. It has a built in fan to keep this cool as it works. It is very quiet and does what is expected. I would recommend this to friends and family.

I was worried that the facial cleansing brush would be too rough on my sensitive skin. It turns out to be okay. I really like the massaging head either before or after I use the sensitive brush to clean my face. I usually spend 10-15 minutes cleaning the makeup off of my face after a long working day. Now, I can just use this LumaRx facial cleansing brush for less than 5 minutes to clean and remove the makeup. It's really easy to use and simple enough for anyone with a busy schedule to get a deep clean for a short period of time. This is a great massaging / make-up removal tool and all the girls in the family love it. It looks, feel very professional and the charges hold well - at least from initial usage. The concern is with replacement heads, as another type of facial brush we have has a larger connector than this one. So far we could not find LumaRx replacement heads at their lumarx dotcom website or here on amazon. The connection is made via a small pentagon shaped connection, and that pentagon has the side of just under 3/16 inches - so it is relatively small. Other than that, great product. Fantastic facial cleaning brush. I like that it has a pretty case to use if I ever travel with it. You can store the other brushes (comes with 3. One for massage, one for sensitive skin and one normal brush)
Great that the battery holds a charge for about 30 uses. Nice feature for when I'm on the road and don't want to bother with the charger at every hotel.
Has 3 speeds so you can decide on how much brushing you want on your face.
My face feels so clean after I'm done using it. I put on some night cream, with the massage brush, afterwards and my face is so smooth. I love it.
I'm also wondering how difficult it will be to find replacement brush heads. I'm pretty happy about the LumaRx facial cleansing brush. It is designed very ergonomically and is very comfortable to hold during use. The tool is extremely lightweight and has a tapered design which makes it so comfortable to use. The instructions are to use it for a minute each morning and evening. It has illustrations which show you to spend 20 seconds on the right side and 20 seconds on the left side and 20 seconds on the T-zone. The tool will actually buzz gently when you should move to the next area. This is a great feature! It also comes with 3 brush heads; massage, sensitive and normal skin. I am using the sensitive for now and it is perfect for a gentle exfoliation. When I am finished with that minute, my skin just glows and feels so clean! Hopefully the heads do not need replaced quickly as I do not think they are yet available on Amazon or online. It also comes with a sleek charger that does not take up any room at all on the counter – this is important to me as I have a small bathroom. Also, the LumaRx comes with a very nice carrying case that will come in handy for an upcoming vacation. After moistening my face and the brush heads with water, I tested the sensitive and normal heads with both soap and [[ASIN:B01648QDS4 L'Oreal Paris Age Perfect Facial Cream Cleanser, 5 Fluid Ounce]] and the massaging head with water alone. After a one-minute "application" with any one of the brushes, I love how smooth and clean this makes my face feel.

The packages includes:

- three brush heads (sensitive, normal, and massage) and their covers which have air vents to hasten drying
- one charging base with power cord
- one brush wand that operates at 3 speed levels
- one white plastic zippered travel case
- one instruction pamphlet

PROS:

- The wand contains a rechargeable battery that last for 30 uses. The first charge takes up to six hours. It also has a 30 minute fast-charge feature that will provide 4-5 uses. By the way, I love the charging light on the base; it has a "cool" factor to it.

- There's a one minute timer that has what I call a "tripacer" (like Sonicare's quadpacer) timer built in for each of the three zones of the face. These zones are the T zone, left side, and right side. What this means is that the unit pauses ever so slightly ever twenty seconds to let the user know when it's time to move on to the next zone so that the cleaning time can be distributed evenly among zones.

- None of the three brushes were rough or extremely abrasive. The rotating and vibrating brush heads were as gentle as could be and I have sensitive skin.

- The wand with brush can be used in the shower as long as it's not fully submerged in water.

- This can be used to remove cosmetics.

- The unit comes with a 2-year limited warranty.

CONS:

- Although these brushes remove make-up effectively, I personally only like to use this on the days I do not wear makeup. The reason is that the eye area has to be avoided. I use eye makeup so I wind up washing my entire face with my hands instead as it does not make sense to me to use a brush on only part of my face.

- There are a lot of don'ts in the manual like don't submerge in water, don't use around the eyes, don't use if you are taking steroid-based medication, don't operate outdoors or where there are aerosol products or oxygen being administered, etc.

- If used daily at no more than the maximum two times per day, the brush heads need to be replaced every three months. The Massaging head (since it doesn't not have bristles) can be replaced every six months. This can get expensive. I contacted the company for the replacement price and they said they would let me know when it's orderable on Amazon. I will update the comments section of this review with that information when I receive it.

- The battery on this unit is NOT replaceable as per the email from them which I posted in the comments section of this review.

To begin, we did get a discount for these tweezers if we promised to write a review about them; however the stipulation was that the review had to be honest, so..it is! This tweezer set is hands down the best I've seen outside of an operating room. My dad is a surgeon and my mom is a nurse so growing up I always had really good tweezers and other instruments to use for the occasional splinter etc... When I moved away from home I noticed that good tweezers and such were almost impossible to obtain unless you wanted to pay a fortune for the ones they actually use in operating rooms. The main issue I have with most tweezers is: 1) the metal at the pinching end does not align properly and thus you cannot get a good grip on a hair or splinter and 2) they are made of soft metal and therefore lack the rigidity that is required to get a good grip on the splinter or object.
THESE tweezers are awesome however! The pinching ends meet up perfectly so that if you close the tips together in front of a light, no light comes through, translating into a solid grip. The metal itself is strong and rigid as well, taking care of my second complaint with most tweezers. There is a nice glossy coating on the tweezers which makes them easy to clean and provides a good surface so your fingers don't slip off.
There are four different tweezers included and they are all great. The case it comes in is about the size of a typical wallet. The case is actually pretty tough and it has some sort of velvet like finish on the inside, where the tweezers are. The case will fold in half to make it very compact, even with the tweezers inside. Exactly the kind of tweezer set I was looking for. This set of 4 tweezers is precise and convenient. Definitely happy with my purchase. I am a sucker for beauty implements and I love, love, love this set of tweezers! They are high quality and are comparable to another well known tweezer brand that would cost a person four times what this one cost if four pairs of tweezers were purchased. These came in a nice little pouch with a sealable flap and four individual pockets for the tweezers. This will allow them to be carried easily in a purse or bag and will help prevent them from becoming too dull or the tips from getting bent.

The tweezers are painted with a black sparkly enamel and numbered individually. The company makes ten distinct varieties of tweezers and the package mentions these are the four most popular. There are two pairs of tweezers that are needle sharp which would be great for splinters or ingrown hairs. I used the flat edged tweezers, one of which is slightly slanted. Personally, I do better with the slanted but both worked to remove stray eyebrow hairs quickly and effectively. One of the needle sharp pairs features a curved tip, something I have never seen in any facial tweezers before. I have seen it in industrial picks, but it makes for an effective beauty implement as well.

These tweezers were easily cleaned both before and after use. A quick daub with an alcohol soaked cotton ball did the trick. I would not leave these out in the reach of children as they are sharp (as mentioned earlier). Even the flat edged pairs have a nice edge to them and they are not the typical dime store tweezers that are somewhat blunted.

The customer service I received from Smarkle was enthusiastic. They are proud of their product and very proud that I have gotten it. One thing I was somewhat disappointed in was that there is no mention of getting the tweezers resharpened or reshaped in the event of bending. The other more expensive brand of tweezers provides this service. If Smarkle did, that would push their products over the top for me. But, that may be why the one brand is four times more expensive than Smarkle.

read this article to make an informed decision:
What Is Skin Bleaching?

Skin bleaching is a cosmetic treatment to reduce the prominence of skin discolorations and even out the color of the skin. You can buy bleaching creams over the counter and by prescription.

Some people apply skin lightener to their entire body to change their complexion, but this can be very risky. The active ingredient in some skin lighteners is mercury, so bleaching can lead to mercury poisoning.

Mercury is a toxic agent that can cause serious psychiatric, neurological, and kidney problems. Pregnant women who use a skin lightener with mercury can pass the mercury to their unborn child.

The use of mercury as an ingredient in skin lighteners is banned in the U.S. However, some skin lighteners produced outside the U.S. may still contain mercury.
How Do Skin Lighteners Work?

Skin lighteners contain an active ingredient or a combination of ingredients that reduces the amount of melanin in the skin where it is applied.

How Do Skin Lighteners Work? continued...

The most widely used ingredient in skin lighteners sold in the U.S. is hydroquinone.

The FDA regulates the use of hydroquinone in the U.S. Over-the-counter skin lighteners can contain up to 2% hydroquinone. Dermatologists can write prescriptions for lighteners that contain 4%-6% hydroquinone.

It's important to check with your doctor before using a product with hydroquinone and to follow the doctor's directions exactly.

Other skin lighteners use drugs such as steroids and retinoic acid, which comes from vitamin A, as active ingredients. And some skin lighteners use natural ingredients such as kojic acid -- a compound that comes from a fungus -- and arbutin, a compound found in various plants.
Risks of Skin Lighteners

One of the most significant risks of using some skin lighteners is the potential exposure to mercury. One study found that nearly 1 out of every 4 skin lighteners made in Asia and sold outside the U.S. contained mercury.

There are other potential risks of skin lighteners. Those risks can include the following:

Prolonged use can contribute to premature aging of skin.
Long-term use may increase the risk of skin cancer from sun exposure. Always use sunscreen when using a skin lightener and going out in the sun.
Steroids in some skin lighteners may increase risk for skin infections, skin thinning, acne, and poor wound healing.
Applying steroids to large areas of skin may put you at risk for health problems related to steroid being absorbed by the body.
Hydroquinone may cause unwanted and untreatable skin discoloration (ochronosis).

Let me start by saying that I really like the New York Biology brand of skin care products. Much of what they produce is on the cutting edge of scientific research. I am a huge fan of transgenic pharming so do not think my opinion is based on that. And although this I feel is a good cream for Acne prone skin, the actual scar removal benefits may be lacking.
EGF ( Epidermal growth factor) Is a cytokine (chemicals our cells use to communicate with each other) There are many however EGF helps repair damage to the skin. (Yes this is a real thing and it works, but it needs to get to where is needs to be effective). I was debating on how complicated to make this review because It took me 3 hours and a call to a specialist to help me form my opinion of this product, but most people do not want or require extensive data.
Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF) is a 6.2 kDa polypeptide, It is not huge but is to large to absorbe properly. Your body makes and delivers EGF from the inside so this absorption factor is null. Assuming that any topically applied EGF reaches the dermis, it would be a minute fraction of that applied, and thus not likely to affect collagen production. Also, wrinkle reduction requires not just the making of new collagen, but also the breakdown and disposal of old collagen. That is the role of a different group of cytokines (growth factors), and their target cells, some of which are phagocytes (immune cells that gobble up debris and export it).
So no I do not believe despite the great innovative ingredients that this will be a miracle cure for my acne scars, but It will provide a great moisturizer for acne prone skin. There is a lot of science to back that up, but we don't have all day.

My hair has lots of different kinds of curls in it, from tight coils near the nape of my neck, to spirals, all the way to slightly wavy hair at the crown of my head. I get a more consistent curl when I use curlers! I've been using large foam curlers for a while to get large, uniform waves that straighten out over a few days, but I wanted to try a curler that would give me tighter curls.

The Ohuhu Twist Flex Rods come with 7 different curl sizes, and each size has 6 rollers. The rollers are color-coded by size, so you think I'd be able to find all 7 curlers, but apparently I thought there were only 6 when I took the picture. I'd never used these kinds of curlers before, but they were simple to use. I used the two largest sizes, and took a small section of hair and put the end of it in the middle of a roller. Then, I rolled the hair up into the roller, making sure to keep the hair in the center of the rod. Twisting the ends together keeps the curler in place.

I tried to let my hair air-dry with the curlers in, but I have a LOT of hair, and knew that could take days, so after a few hours, I put on my bonnet dryer and finished the job. I was pretty happy with my ringlets! I did muss them up for a nice, beachy curly-wave, too. I really liked getting the curl all the way to my crown, and how much lift it gave the top of my 'do. And, the curls weren't tangly like my hair can get if I let it completely air dry. I could run my fingers through them and get a messy, beachy wave - and still no frizz or tangles.

(I received this product for review purposes. My opinions are my own. For more information and pictures, please see my blog, Lit From Within.) These flexi-rods are essentially the same as those that you would purchase at your local beauty supply store. The thing I like about the Ohuhu pack is that you have seven varying sizes and colors. There are six of each size. It also comes with the storage bag, as shown, which is great for storage and if you need to travel with them. They run about $13, as of the date of this review. The price isn't bad at all.

These are great if you want spiral curls or to add curls to the ends of your hair. If you are looking to do a full-body style, start at the back of your neck (nape) and use the smaller rods, working your way up to the bigger rods when you get to the middle and top of your hair.

They are super easy to use and because they are soft, it is not too difficult to sleep in.

Of note, I was sent these flex-rods directly, at a discounted rate, in exchange for my honest opinion. My first time buying foam rollers was from Walmart, a pack of 18 conair rollers that came in 2 sizes for $15.. I was pretty disappointed when I saw this pack of 42 for $13 on amazon a few weeks after.

First, the sturdiness of these rods differ from the Conair ones I had purchased. They felt less firm, but found as you go down in size that changes. This can affect how well it stays in your hair, but I just use an elastic on the bottom part to keep my ends rolled.
Second, I have long hair so I found these to be a good length. Also, I combine the purple and blues together when needed, or the yellow and oranges (not very far in sizes and in case 6 isn't enough). I haven't tried the smaller sizes, but that's because I like bigger waves/curls.

I'm not much of a girly girl, so I found these perfect to do my hair the night before. Plus, no heat damage!! In the morning, I take them out, give my hair a few tosses and run my fingers through the curls and done. It may look a little silly at first, but give the hair a few moments to relax.

**Sleeping in them: I found the blues and purples to be the most comfortable, probably because they have the most cushion. Try not to roll to close to the scalp, some hairs might get rolled too tightly and are a pain in the ass when trying to sleep.

- For the girls not having success, you have to use it on damp hair! I've been rolling them in dry hair and then using a spray bottle to wet my hair then wrap them up in a scarf or shirt. I sleep in them and remove in the morning.

I admit that I felt silly buying this...but I HATE to blow-dry my hair because I have very thick, wavy, and frizz-prone hair. So usually when I blow-dry it, I can't use the brush properly like a hairdresser would to really work the frizz out and dry it properly and it ends up look dry and poofy until the next day when it settles down. I typically let my hair just wet-dry and then style with some cream and a curling iron to smooth my ends. But when I saw this, I just had to try it despite having a small bathroom and thinking "do you really want that thing hanging on you wall?" The answer is..."Not really, but I really want a free hand to dry my hair."

So I bought it. Although I was still really unsure about the safety of sectioning this thing to my wall. I imagined it crashing down and smashing my toiletries, injuring the cat, or crashing onto someone's head. I wondered why I decided to buy it. But then I received it in the mail, opened it, and was really surprised at how incredibly heavy and solid this thing is. Everytime I buy a product that is supposed to "suction" and be strong....it isn't. Well, this one is REALLY strong.

I first tested it by suctioning it to the wall (not the mirror as shown in the ad) and left it there for about 2 days just to see if there was any sliding, slipping, or loosening. I pulled HARD on it various ways to try to get it to fall down. This thing is 100% solid and the suction is super-strong. If it stuck to my painted wall, this would never come off a mirror! Then after I inspected it a good bit, bent the arm around, tried out the bungee, and figured out which way the holder that the blow-dryer goes in is supposed to go....I placed my hair dryer in it. I had a hard time, at first getting my dryer to fit because I still had the holder upside down. If the large bolt is pressing against the back of your dryer, it's upside down and it won't seat properly and the bungee will be super-hard to clip (or not at all). So I was like "great this thing doesn't fit my dryer". But you have to twist and move it around to figure out which way yours fits and then it's all pretty much smooth sailing from there.

The "arm" that bends is also really hard to bend and very solid and thick. Merely bumping it (which I did several times), walking into it, or yanking your dryer around doesn't make this flop around. It requires two hands to bend and stays firmly in whatever position you place it for drying. Keep in mind this means that other than minor adjustments, if you need to totally change the dryer position while drying...you will need to take a second to move the arm and reposition it a bit, which is not a one-handed job. I really like that about this. When I finally tried using it after my shower (after days of leaving it hang up to ensure it doesn't fall, playing around with it, and letting my family get used to it being in their way because of our small bathroom) I was delighted that when I moved the dryer lower to blow straight at me....it stayed firmly in place, even after accidentally slapping it with my hairbrush and hands several times. I moved it into a "downward" blowing position about halfway through to get the back and was able to not only use a brush and my hands like a normal person, but I noted that I was able to get my hair dry in half the normal time (I assume because of extra brushes and hands). My hair even looked less frizzy and more like what it should look like after I go to the salon! My significant other came home and laughed when he saw me awkwardly using it and trying to position it right....but he thinks it's cool, too.

It made my life much easier and really DOES function like a permanent fixture if you want it to. I plan to leave mine up all of the time for ease of use rather than redoing the suction and placement each time. It's easy to just take the arm and push it up really high when you're done, take the dryer out of it, and it's out of the way of anyone walking through, opening cabinets, etc until next time you want to use it.

This is a pretty innovative product and I don't feel like I wasted money on it because it has made a loathsome part of my beauty routine easier...even if it did make my bathroom just slightly uglier :-)

In all seriousness, if you have space or really hate trying to use a brush and properly dry your hair, this is worth it. If I had more storage nearby, I'd probably take it down in between uses because it really is easy to suction and adjust once you understand what goes where and how it works. I had fun trying this out and using it on my hair and plan to keep on using it in the future. It's an odd device, for sure...but doesn't hesitate if you're worried it will be "cheap" or flimsy. This thing could be a deadly weapon, it's so heavy and clearly intended to stay in place. If that's what you need in a dryer holder, absolutely buy this. I don't regret my purchase and I doubt you will, either. I hope you found my review to contain useful information and I am happy to answer any questions you may have. Thanks for reading and happy styling!!

This is a blend of effective natural whitening agents with additional properties beneficial for skin. These ingredients have been demonstrated to even skin tone, lighten hyperpigmentation, build collagen and inhibit the production of melanin. The skin lightening agents in this product are as follows. Google each for further information, but in brief summary:

Glutathione has been called the mother of all anti-oxidants. Clinical research has shown glutathione significantly lowers the skin's melanin content in as little as 10 weeks.

Kojic acid is derived from mushrooms, used as a skin lightening agent because it inhibits the protein tyrosinase from producing melanin. Kojic acid alone has shown effects faster than most other lightening agents, beginning at about 6 weeks.

Even faster is Artocarpus Lakoocha Heartwood extract. Used alone, it has shown significant whitening effect after only 4 weeks of application.

Coenzyme Q10 aka ubiquinone is a chemical substance naturally produced by our own cells. Applied topically, it can help lighten freckles, age spots, acne scars, and other discolourations. Q10 may also help enhance regeneration of skin cells, thereby reducing the appearance of wrinkles.

Vitamin C provides surprisingly high level lightening and increased UV protection while helping to fade sun/age spots and freckles. Vitamin C is also proven to boost glutathione levels which further helps lighten skin. It also enhances collagen synthesis and increases cell turnover, which makes it a popular ingredient in anti-aging serums.

All together this should be effective in treating melasma (dark pigmentation), acne scars, freckles and age spots. The company does not mention SPF but the inclusion of titanium dioxide, coenzyme Q10 and vitamin C would be expected to provide some degree of UV protection.

Before applying whitening lotion, you should perform a patch test. This is a good practice before using any skin care product, but especially those containing parabens. (common allergen) Just dab a little on your wrist or inner elbow and wait a few minutes. If you experience any signs of irritation such as redness, itch, or swelling, of course discontinue use.

This little machine is just amazing! It's so quiet you can't tell that it's on until you touch it to your nail. There's no vibration in either the hand tool or the unit. There is the option to control the speed by hand or a foot pedal. For myself, in a non professional manner, I'll stick to controlling the speed by hand. So I'll have no information regarding the foot pedal.

Controlling speed by hand is really easy. The bar you move to the right, to increase the speed, or left, to decrease it, gives you better control than the defined/set speeds (e.g. low/med/high).

The hand tool is a bit heavy feeling, but that's most likely due to the metal casing and most of the interior parts. This is not enough weight to interfere with its use. The chuck is easy to operate and it's simple to change drill bits as desired. The cord is a nice length and gives you decent room to work in.

The accessories that came with this unit are quite nice. I won't need to buy sanders for a looong time. You get three bags with about 100 sanders in each bag and each bag being a different grit. There are extra drill bits and it's a nice selection of bits in different shapes and sizes. There's no guide to tell you which bit to use for what, so it's trial and error and what your preference is.

I like the way the hand tool connects to the unit, by way of a 5-pin connecter. I had one unit where it was connected via a 2-pin connection. This shorted out and my husband had to hard wire it to the machine.

There were basic instructions for operating the machine. But again, nothing for the bits. I've just been experimenting with them, see how they work and which ones I like.

So aside from that little annoyance, I love this little machine, it's a joy to use. I've had a couple of different machines in the past and they didn't last long.

I have high hopes for this unit. The solid construction and materials it's made from are far superior than most other units out there (within this price range). I highly recommend this unit and would buy it again should the need ever arise.

My husband has never been able to use electric shavers because they irritate his skin. I thought we would give this one a try and he is thrilled with it. No break outs and it gives him a close, clean shave. The battery stays charged for days of use and you can use it wet or dry. Excellent product. This is a “dressed up” version of the Wahl “LifeProof” shaver (which I also reviewed). It has a more upscale look and feel to it, plus adds a battery gauge to show the charge level. However, the shave quality is the same – OK, but not a standout.

The case feels more solid than the LifeProof and, while it’s more of a traditional look, I think they did a nice job with the overall aesthetics. It is pretty grippy even with wet hands. It does not, however, feel as comfortable to hold as the more sculpted models such as most of the Panasonic shavers and some Braun shavers.

The shave quality of this model is identical to that of the LifeProof: very Remington in how it feels (close, but rather aggressive). Performance is best on the easy spots (cheek) but not as good on the more trickier spots (neck and jawline). The flex head helps with dealing with face contours but it lacks enough travel to do an excellent quality job.

The aggressiveness of the shave is dialed down when using it wet. It needs a very, very thin layer of shave cream (the gel style creams work well) or the head gets bogged down.

Love the trimmer! The positioning could be improved to make it easier to use, but it cuts very cleanly on sideburns and ‘shash trimming.

The controls are clean, easy to read and tell you all you need to know (charge and battery status).

I like the feel of this better than the Wahl LifeProof, but the shave quality keeps this at the same rating (average, which is 3 stars). It’s a very workable shaver, but for the price there are better choices available from Panasonic (anything in their Arc line) or, for less money, from Remington. Very advanced looking razor. However the clipper on back is somewhat oddly placed and the razor does not give a very close shave. It will do but I bought a very old Panasonic razor at a yard sale for 2 bucks once that gave a closer shave. I have not used this under wet conditions so I really cannot vouch for that. If I wet my face I am going to put shaving cream on it and use a powerless razor. My husband is very happy with this razor. I think of Wahl as a hair clipper and probably wouldn't have thought of them when replacing his razor, but I am glad to have learned that they make just as good of a quality razor. He uses a regular razor in the shower, then runs an electric around to catch any missed spots. Because of this the battery doesn't need to be charged very often. The battery life indicator is very helpful as is the razor's ability to charge very quickly. He likes it. He is not raving about it being the best razor ever, but we are both happy with this unit. I've tried electric razors in the past, but always end up going back to a traditional razor (currently using Harry's razors), but I've stuck with the Wahl Smart Shave for a couple weeks now. You have to temper your expectations with an electric razor. You're trading the closeness of the shave for the convenience. You can do a dry shave at home or on the go, fairly quickly with no mess. My face feels a bit like a five o'clock shadow, from the jump, but looks well-kept and neat. The addition of the detail razor is really cool. It's a bit oddly tacked on to the side of the razor, but works very well and is easy enough to manage. I also do like the lithium ion battery and battery gauge for keeping an eye on when you need to bring out the charging cable. 90 minutes of 'shaving' time is pretty generous and even after a few weeks the gauge still reads full. My husband usually does not like electric shavers but he likes this one. Normally he uses a non-disposable razor with a badger brush but he does like to have this one on hand for quick in between shaves. It gives him a close shave without giving him a razor burn feeling. Leaves his skin nice and smooth. It holds a charge well, too. Wahl is a great brand and you know you're getting quality that will last a long time. I would recommend this shaver to anyone. It would make a great gift, too! I have very thick, very coarse hair growth on my face. Shaving and I have never been friends. I usually can only use a Mach III blade 2 times (3 times max) before I have to throw it away, else it turns my face into blood salad.

As such, electric shavers have never done that good of a job on my face. I always use an electric shaver first to get the big chunks of hair off so that the Mach III can go in for precision, but in no way shape or form can I use an electric shaver alone and then go out into public. This is especially true of the neck area.

For years, I've been using the Norelco line of shavers (most recently the 3000) as my choice. The three-circle-blades-in-a-triangle works best for me, especially on that stubborn neck area. It isn't necessarily the closest shave, but it does get the most hair removed overall. And its usable in the shower.

Enter this Wahl shaver. Right out the gate, I'll say that on the parts it does shave properly (flat open areas like sideburns), it cuts super close. It also charges very quickly, behaves well in the shower, and is easy to clean. But that doesn't really set it apart, since many shavers also do this. I like the carry bag it comes with.

What I don't like is that it does REALLY bad work on the curved parts of the face such as the aforementioned neck area. In fact, it's almost useless there. I had to clean up with the Norelco after using the Wahl, and I did several test runs. The Wahl performed a little bitter with shaving cream, but then again, so does the Norelco.

Maybe if your face isn't gnarly and coarse like mine, this Wahl is for you. But I can't really recommend it for guys like me when there are better, cheaper options available. First of all, there is a sticker over the charging lights, so you will want to remove that.

My shaver came pre-charged, which was nice.

Speaking of charging, one thing this shaver is missing is a cradle for charging. You have to plug it in. Not that big of a deal, but it would have been nice to have a cradle.

Overall, it’s a very nice shaver. It’s comfortable to hold, and smooth. No “pulling” of hairs. It has two shaver heads. A lot of the less expensive models have only one. I haven’t had any issues with “loose hairs” either – hairs that it doesn’t cut.

I like that you can wash it with water.

For the price, I don’t see that much difference between this one and a couple of the other Wahl models, which are lower in price.

One thing that this one is missing. . . a way to “lock” it for travel, so that it will not accidently turn-on when something presses against it. It really should have that at this price. I had a set of Wahl clippers that lasted for over a decade. I finally got a new pair of clippers and through the old clippers away. ORIGINAL REVIEW: Only used the steamer once so far, but it took me 20 minutes just to remove the gel from ONE fingernail. I had to fix the accent nail on one hand when I chipped the nail, but didn't have the same color that the salon used. So, I was taking the color off the accent nail on the other hand so that my accent nails would match. Anyway, the plastic insert that holds the acetone doesn't fit snugly in the machine. It's plastic, so when you put it in the steamer, it pops up just a little. I added a little pressure to push it back down, but as soon as I took my hands off of it, it popped back up again. So, I don't know if it can actually make enough contact with the machine to get warm enough to create enough steam or not. I did have to refill the reservoir twice for that one nail though, and the polish crumbled off... never got moist. Ended up having to file the rest off and then buffing the nail. The lights on the machine aren't consistent either. When I first turned it on, the H (Heat) light came on. When the S (Steam) light came on, I put one finger in and curled it around the part that it shows in videos on-line, and I rested the remainder of the fingers across the top of the steamer. I noticed that the light kept bouncing back and forth between the H to the S. I checked the cord/plug to make sure everything was tight. No issues there. So, I don't think that's normal and feel like I've wasted my money. I was wary about this product due to all the negative reviews, but thought I'd take my chances. $30+ is a lot of money to "waste." Disappointed. Amazing! As described and works very well. Less hassle! fast shipping awesome I just received the unit and used it for the first time. It gets very very hot to the point that I can't keep my fingers in the unit. I bought this being a bit skeptical about removing other than gel polish. I was willing to take that chance vs drying out my fingertips with messy wraps and taking an hour. This works! I e-file off the shiny top coat, steam for 10 min. A beep will sound at 5 and 10 minutes. I start using my steel pusher and also file off softened product. I repeat this 2-3 times and my nails are product free, and not dried out! The unit itself it pretty simple, but does a great job. I like it, however it does take longer t remove the polish. I find that this does take a bit longer than 10 minutes but it does work and I do like it. It certainly is an improvement from the cotton balls and foil wraps. EDIT 02/28/2019: As we all know there is no "quick" way of taking off gel nail polish. The one thing I have noticed and "do like" about this machine is you do not have to scrape or file off the left over polish. It does peel nicely. Patience is the key to success with this product. Also certain brands of polish come off easier than others.

Unless you do your own watch service it's easier and cheaper to just buy another brand new one. Basically the only mechanical watches that make economic sense to own are the very high end watches that will not only keep their value but actually appreciate so the service costs are offset by the appreciation. I'm in the process of ridding myself of my Seiko and Citizen mechanical divers but I will keep my Rolex Sub because it is already worth far more than I paid for it.

With all that said I was on the quest for a good quality quartz diver and looked at Omega and Heuer. Lots of people look down their noses at quartz movements but remember this, when it comes time to service your $250 automatic Seiko and it costs $200+, you can simply replace the Ronda movement in this Phoibos watch and you're good for another 10-15 years. Most quartz divers use movements made by others (even the higher end stuff) and the movements are incredibly cheap and durable. Even the Omega Seamaster quartz Diver uses an $80 ETA movement. So unlike the high end mechanical watches that use in house movements there really is little difference, at least regarding the movement, when it comes to quartz divers. So the question becomes, do I pay $2000 for an Omega Seamaster with an $80 Swiss quartz movement or pay $120 for a Phoibos with a $25 Swiss quartz movement?

I can say this will full confidence; this Phoibos watch gives up NOTHING to the Omega Seamaster. The finish is surprisingly perfect. I expected the quality to be like that of any mid-level Seiko or Citizen but boy was I pleasantly surprised. The quality really is hard to believe. A sapphire crystal, solid end links on a perfectly polished and brushed bracelet, case polishing equal to ANY watch and a Swiss quartz movement, all for just $120! If you want one of these you'd better get it before someone comes to their senses and starts selling these for what they are truly worth. I initially thought I had simple/easily found criteria for a new hair dryer, but I had trouble meeting them. Based on my previous hair dryer ownership, I noticed there were 2 failures that would come up first, switch failure or motor fan failure. My criteria was looking for a switch that operates like a toggle switch and had the 2 speeds on either end of the off position (LOW - OFF - HIGH). My reasoning for the switches is that the sliding type switch tends to wear out faster. Less cycling of the switch to reach the HIGH setting increases my chance of longer ownership. My other criteria is that it needs to have an AC type motor, rather than the cheaper/low durability DC motor. This hair dryer met them all!

I spent a few days before purchasing this particular silicone sponge set or any kind of silicone sponge set for that matter, but, I am very glad that I decided to give it a try! With few reviews and real life photos of the items from the customers, I hesitated to decide on ScionBeauty's sponge, but, I am a satisfied customer for the following reasons.

First of all, this is a great value for a set of 5 sponges (2 beauty blender and 3 silicone sponges). The size is not too small nor big and is perfect. Upon opening the package, I recommend washing all sponges. At least the silicone sponges. I used a very very small amount of nice hand soap and very gently washed and rinsed them well. Here are what I noticed about and did with each sponge.

** BEAUTY BLENDER:
The beauty blender indeed expand in size! I would say about 2.5 times the original size. I washed it yesterday and squeezed out excess water with a towel to make sure it doesn't build up mold inside. It did shrink, but, is still bigger than the unwashed one. And, it certainly did NOT become stiff or rip, which I was initially worried about. It became very slightly harder than the unwashed one, but, the washed one is still MUCH bouncier compared to the unwashed one. I actually like this medium level of softness/stiffness. Another reason why I hesitated to wash the blender is because I read some reviews about an inexpensive blender bleeding out pink dye. That is not the case at all about this ScionBeauty blender. At that point, I felt very comfortable using this product. When you wash it, you do need to rinse thoroughly to remove soap bubbles. If soap residue remains in the blender, the blender probably will disintegrate over time and it won't be good for your skin either. Upon arrival, the blender has a very faint smell to it. But, it does go away next day if you keep it out of a plastic bag that it comes in. Also, once you wash it, the smell completely goes away.

** SILICONE SPONGE:
It feels good against the skin! It curves well when I try to bend to fit the curves of my face, so, I can say this particular sponge is flexible. It curves but bounces back is a good way to describe it, I think. On the back side of the plastic bag this sponge set comes in, there is a sticker attached - "How to use ScionBeauty Silicone sponge." I read the instructions as well as referred to Youtube videos and online tips. You do need to dab and pat on your skin rather than glide along on your skin as they say. Then, you can successfully apply a thin and natural looking layer of liquid foundation. I like the natural look, so, this silicone sponge works well for me. Do not remove the sealing (a thin layer of silicone on the edge of the sponge). You need to use the raised side of the sponge to put foundation or any other makeup item on. I used the liquid foundation, but, all I needed was about the size (amount) of a rice grain or two and it covered about a half of my face. It did not smear (Again, dab and tap!). After I finished applying liquid foundation on my face, I again washed the silicone sponge with a very small amount of hand soap and dried with a towel. I also used the silicone sponge to apply serum and it did work extremely well. I always wasted too much with my hands soaking up the serum more than my facial skin did.

This may be a makeup fad that goes away before too long, but, I'm sure I will be using this sponge set for a long time. It was a bit disappointing that I did not receive a reply from the seller when I contacted about the warranty they mention on the Amazon product page, but, I'm sure this product will last long enough to worth the price, so, I'm ok with that in this case and decided not to deduct a star from my review. The product itself and its value still deserve 5 stars in my mind. I highly recommend this sponge set for those who are hesitating to try. It may not be your kind of item, but, if used right and if you happen to like the texture of the sponges, you will understand what I'm talking about.

I'm posting real life photos (not photoshopped, I mean) of the product, so that you can see how the sponges actually look like and how big/small they are. The sponge set does not come in a cute bag or case as you can see, but, it is good enough for yourself and casual gifting.

Have been using brush and soap to shave since I was on my first Submarine in '77 and still use them. Bought this soap in June of 2014 and ordering my replacement today April, 2014 and still have about a month or two left on the original. Very foamy, smooth, and last a long time. Yes it is more than the cheap stuff, but by now I would have gone through 10 or 12 cakes of the cheap stuff. You cannot go wrong with this soap for comfort, smooth shave, and lasting a long time. This review will be somewhat bi-polar, but this soap truly performs that way for me.

A quick TL;DR for those who don't want too many details: It gives an amazing post shave and lathers quickly, but that lather dissipates when created with hard water.

Onto the nitty-gritty. I have a plethora of artisan shaving soaps from the likes of Stirling, Mike's, Barrister & Mann, Catie's Bubbles, WSP, Razorock, etc... I also use some classic mass produced software like TOBS, Arko, Proraso, and some others. While I do like certain products more than others, I can typically get a quality shave from any of the products mentioned, and any of the razors I keep in rotation. However, I purchased Mitchell's Wool Fat because I had a specific need: a utilitarian soap that can protect me while I'm shaving my head. I typically only shave my head every 7-14 days (yes, this is absolutely doable with the right razors) so the job tends to require quality lather. I get great results from most of my artisan soaps, but the job is more time-consuming when I have to load up my brush from a container or the like. Creams work okay in terms of convenience, but they are a notch less protective than the artisan soaps. Another side note: I've veered more into fragrances in the form of EDT/cologne/EDP recently, so unscented shaving products are a plus for me these days. MWF and Arko both smell like cheap hotel soaps to me, and I have no problem with that.

I wanted a mug soap that could just live in a big, flat soup mug and be on standby for those head shaves. My first attempt at doing this simply and cheaply was with Arko. I crammed some into a salsa bowl, and it worked great for whipping up a large volume of lather very quickly. However, Arko loses its slickness when the lather isn't of the thicker variety, and it tends to function better as a cushiony soap. Yes, I'm aware that I can cram an artisan soap into whatever container I want, but I prefer to save those products (and their fancy scents) for when I'm savoring a more luxurious shave. I also wanted to try something that is triple-milled, very hard, and will sit properly in a mug without requiring pressing or manipulation, much how people used Williams and Old Spice back in the day.

Enter MWF. I knew this soap's reputation, and I knew that I was working with hard water, but I wanted to give it a go anyways because it's a classic that I'd never tried. This soap produces lather quite readily, actually. I tried it with synthetic, boar, and badger brushes. I always used as much product as possible, and bloomed the soap by soaking it in the mug during my shower. However, I'd always get similar results without fail. A very good-looking lather will be produced, and it will always begin to dissipate within seconds. Thicker lather? Dissipates. Thinner and more voluminous lather? Dissipates. Every time.

Fortunately, I still found it usable, because WOW this lather was incredibly slick, even after its partial dissipation. You can easily go over spots several times, especially if you apply some water to that spot. This slickness did a sufficient job of protecting my dome against cuts, but unfortunately there tends to be a bit more irritation and aftershave burn (nothing too excessive) due to the fact that this lather has insufficient cushion while being used with very aggressive razors. I tried to mitigate this by only lathering up sections of my head, then repeating that over and over to prevent the dissipation. This helped a bit, but the inconvenience was enough where I've unfortunately chosen to oust MWF from the very role I purchased it to fill.

This may read like a 1-2 star review, but here comes the good part. MWF, despite it's dissipating lather, repeatedly left me with the absolute best post shave feel I ever experienced. It soundly defeats even my 2 favorite soaps in this category, which are Stirling and B&M. I know that my skin loves lanolin, and I'm guessing the MWF contains a high concentration of lanolin, which unfortunately may contribute to it disagreeing with my hard water. The post shave is a hell of a payoff though, to the point where I'm glad that I tried it.

Bottom line, this product is not for everyone. If you're new to traditional wet shaving, then avoid it in favor of something more simplistic and easy to lather (TOBS, Razorock, or perhaps even Arko). If you know you have hard water, then steer clear unless you're just out to appease your curiosity. Personally, I'm split between disappointment and amazement. The post shave and speed of lather has wowed me enough to hang onto this soap just in case I end up moving somewhere with better water. I can also still use it for a regular face shave, especially with milder razors. However, this soap did end up failing me as a workman-like product that can provide high-end protection. I've since replaced it with a relative newcomer to the soap market, and the only triple-milled artisan soap that I know of: [[ASIN:B01L0ENB3W Fine - American Blend]]. No, it doesn't meet my desire for something unscented, but it does have that incredibly agreeable classic scent of barbasol, and I can't argue with that. A lot has been said about this product. I purchased based solely on its review, it is a good shave soap. Lather is descent and provides good protection and cushion against cuts and irritations.

This wig is great for the money. Here's what I did to get it lay more natural though. Things you'll need: Verb Ghost Dry Oil, liquid concealer one shade lighter than your skin, powder concealer your correct color, eye shadow brush, mascara in the color of your natural hair, clean and dry mascara brush, scissors and tweezers.

1. First I trimmed the lace to match my hairline. (I cut off a good quarter inch of the front hair with the lace, you don't have to do this but it fits my face better this way).
2. Make the split I like on the side. Tweeze away the space in the middle of the split to make this split more noticable. At the front tweeze a triangle starting point also helps with that more natural split.
3. Put liquid concealer on the underside of the split, use eye shadow brush to brush the powder foundation on the top visible part you plucked. (Any extra powder, just shake the wig gently and it will fall away.)
4. I used the brown mascara to accent the roots of the split and roots along the front of the wig.
5. With wig in hand, spray Verb Ghost Dry Oil on the hair, shake and smooth loose hairs and tangles by hand. Synthetic hair will be soft but not shiny anymore.

Green Tea - This mask is for people who deal with excess sebum. That being said, I use this one the most. I bought this because.............

1.) It gets a lot of reviews on YouTube and Lalique seems to get a lot of respect as a company.
2.) It's supposed to be a good example of a Vetiver fragrance
3.) Vetiver seems to be a big category for men's fragrances.
4.) As a newcomer to men's fragrances, I had no idea what Vetiver actually smelled like.
5.) This stuff is widely discounted and it seemed like a low risk option to learn about Vetiver and answer some of my questions.

So how does it smell? Great! I loved it from the first moment of the first spray through the dry down right up until it disappeared on my skin.

Reviewers use words like "dark, brooding, mysterious, and serious" to describe this. I don't get any of that. It just smells good. It makes me happy. No, it's not a light citrus smell for summer days. It's a heavier, richer smell that's probably better for an evening out.

Personally I find this a lot like the Dolce & Gabbana The One EDP I also bought. The smell is totally different but with both these fragrances.........
1.) I just liked the smell from the first moment.
2.) The concentration is Eau De Parfum for both.
3.) The longevity, projection, and sillage seems similar.

And speaking of performance, this is NOT "beast mode" stuff. It's more subtle. And as a newcomer I'm learning that can be a good thing or a bad thing depending on the circumstances when you're wearing it. But for the most part, subtle is safer and understated is the classier way to go. So for both the D&G The One EDP and this Encre Noir A L'Extreme these impress me as grown up fragrances that come off as sophisticated scents for grown men who wear suits for a living. I think this would be out of place on a guy in torn jeans, sneakers, and a tee shirt.

So performance..........
Longevity - I find it's gone in about 5-6 hours. That's fine. I can always respray if I want.
Projection - Maybe arm's length at most. That's OK. It's not "in your face", it's subtle. Someone needs to be within 3 feet to really pick upon it. If you respray after a few hours you won't offend people.
Sillage - Again modest. I really don't see you offending a room full of people as you walk through and leave them choking and gagging.
Uniqueness - This is not your typical men's cologne smell in my limited experience. It's different. It may get people thinking / wondering about what that smell is. In a good way.
Compliments - I've only asked one woman what she thought and I was surprised that she really liked it. A good start.

Personally, I think this lives up to the reviews and the hype. if this is what a good Vetiver cologne smells like, I like it. I haven't tried the original Encre Noir or the Sport version. This L'Extreme version was recommended as the best and most wearable choice and I'm happy I gave it a shot.

Things they don't describe in the mostly worthless manual:

The charging indicator is a steady red AC plug symbol.

The LCD indication at full charge is 99. A RED (not a far more intuitive GREEN) battery full symbol is shown at when the charge reaches 99.

A low battery is indicated by a flashing red AC plug symbol when the charge number on the LCD reaches 10.

Charge time was tested and found to be 82 minutes. The manual claims 60 to 90 minutes, so they got that right.

Use time is specified in the manual as 50 to 60 minutes. The run time was tested and found to be only 30 minutes in 5 minute on, five minute off intervals, just free running and not being used to shave which should further reduce the run time slightly.

The charge indicator was at 52 after 25 minutes and then rapidly dropped from that to 10 only five minutes later causing the low battery indicator to flash, so I would definitely NOT trust the charge indicator to be an accurate indication of how much shaving time you have left. They are apparently not calculating percent charge remaining and displaying it on the LCD, they are simply and far less usefully displaying percent battery VOLTAGE which drops off rapidly at what is called the battery's discharge "knee." A cheap route to take revealing that the LCD display is nothing more useful than a gimmick.

The manual states that the razor should be unplugged from the charger (this razor package does not come with an AC to USB charge adapter) when the charge number reaches 99, so I suspect this charger might not have an intelligent charger which stops the battery charge process at full charge to avoid battery damage over the long term. I watched a YouTube video on how to safely dermaroll/micro-needle at home before doing it, and recommend others do the same. These were my key takeaways:
- soak the head in 91% isopropyl alcohol for 20 minutes before and after using. These needles will puncture the top layer of your skin so they need to be CLEAN.
- wash your face thoroughly with a fragrance-free and oil-free cleanser before rolling.
-roll your face methodically, about 3 swipes back and forth (6 total) per area. Then do the same in the opposite direction (ie. First side to side then up and down).
- DO NOT PUSH DOWN ON THE ROLLER. The needles are sharp enough to penetrate the top layer of your skin with very little pressure. Applying too much pressure can be very damaging.
-try to roll on a flat skin surface by holding your skin taut. Be careful around eyes, sides of nose, and lips.
- after rolling, only apply fragrance-free serum or moisturizer. Don’t use anything that you don’t already know works well with your skin. I have used several electric shavers in my life, all of them being Norelco. I was never a fan of the two-bladed shavers, I grow a thick beard, and it just takes too long to shave with those things. The 3-bladed shavers can be hit or miss depending on brand/model. Norelco used to make quality shavers back in the 80's and 90's. Since Phillips's acquisition of the Norelco brand however, the quality has gone down drastically. Many reviews complain of underpowered motors, motors burning out early, and poor shaving quality, unless of course you buy the high end 200 dollar model, then your in heaven lol.

Thankfully these day, we have a choice. I don't know about you, but I am not in the rich income bracket, I can't just dump 200 dollars into a shaver just to get something that is quality. Fortunately, there are many different types of shavers made in China now, that are much more affordable. What sold me on this shaver, is that it uses a 800MAH lithium rechargeable battery, that can be charged via USB. It uses a pretty blue LED battery indicator display, which shows minutes of run-time remaining.

It uses a standard 3-bladed system, with a pop up side-burn trimmer. It is also easy to pop the blades off and clean them, and even though I didn't require this feature, it is also IPX7 waterproof. The shaver comes with a nice velvet pouch, a brush, USB cable, and a operators manual. When I turned the unit on, I couldn't believe how quiet this thing runs, most certainly quieter then the old 80's - 90's Norelco models. So the question you might be asking is, how does it perform?

If all you have is stubble, you can expect this to provide a pretty smooth shave within a reasonable amount of time. I just did nice and slow rotational movements, as you are supposed to do with this type of shaver, and it did a pretty good job! If you let your beard get beyond a stubble, as one would expect, it does take longer to get the job done, but the shaver was able to do it, and seemed to have enough power, not just in time duration, but also in horse power.

Since I did not do a wet shave with this, I can't speak as to its effectiveness. I bought an electric shaver for the convenience of a dry shave, as wet shaving is a pain in the but for me. While the water proof rating allows one to simply run the head under the water stream to clean it out, I however just used the brush that they supplied, and some canned air, and it did just as good, without fully taking the blades out of the head. Recharge time is faster then they state when utilizing a powerful Anker wall charger that puts out 3 amps. I charged my battery from 45 minutes left, to 60-minutes left, in only 20 minutes.

In conclusion, I believe this to be a very nice electric shaver. And for the price I paid for it, I expected it to be weaker in construction, however, that is further from the truth. The construction of this shaver is top notch, and rivals higher end Phillips Norelco's in my humble opinion. First of all, it doesn't suffer from the two major issues most cheap nail drills face: lack of torque and internal wobbling. A lack of torque is when the rotation mechanism stalls out if you press hard enough against the nail. You'll know a nail drill has internal wobbling because it will almost tickle or feel uncomfortable when you file your nails.

With that being said, here's what I don't like: I prefer much thinner nail drills. It also would be nice for the manufacturer to explain the differences between all the drill bits and what the intended use case is for each one.

FOR THOSE OF YOU THAT CAN'T CHANGE THE DRILL BIT:

Turn the top portion of the drill toward the side labeled "R" until you hear a click (this is important) use pliers and pull out the drill bit. You'll need to use more force than you think.
Once you've removed the drill bit, stop turning the top portion of the drill toward "R". The mechanism will go back to the center by itself. Pick your desired drill bit and put it where the old drill bit was. Turn the top portion of the drill towards the labeled "S" until you hear a click to secure the drill bit (The drill bit WILL fall out if you don't twist it towards "S" until you hear a click). Use: After I washed and conditioned my hair, I applied a leave in conditioner that has a strong scent, as well as a split end repair serum that also has a scent (my normal hair routine, not bc this set was lacking). I used those liberally. The next morning, ALL I could smell was the shampoo, and it was STRONG! I was impressed. It has a pleasant rose scent.

Consistency: Shampoo has a normal medium thickness consistency and lathers well, but doesn't get as sudsy as other commercial shampoos. I'm not used to this and probably used more shampoo than needed. Conditioner also has a normal consistency with it being relatively thick and holding its shape once pumped into the hand (not watery at all). I LOVED the way it made my hair feel while in, and once rinsed. It didn't make my hair feel slimy like other conditioners do, but it made my hair feel soft, in a natural way, if you will. With other conditioners, even if I leave it on for a while as sort of a hair mask, my hair is still super tangly once rinsed. I did not experience that with this conditioner. I was thrilled at this alone because it's a big deal to me since my hair is so thin and brittle. Breakage when brushing will be minimal now due to less tangles.

How it fairs with dyed hair: I have been dying my hair a brightish red for over ten years now, and I have a good bit of experience using shampoos and trying to make my color last. This is my first time using a sulfate free shampoo and I did notice minimal color washout. I was impressed by this as well. And even though it did well in this area, I ALWAYS try to wash out the shampoo and conditioner as soon as possible once on. The longer it sits in my hair, the more color washes out. But that's just a given. I really do feel this shampoo and conditioner set will help with washout as it is sulfate free, and that plays a huge part with colored hair.

Packaging: I was less than impressed with this because, just as others stated, it did leak. But it leaked because the pumps were not pressed in and locked, as lotions and other items with pumps come. I'm not even sure that the pumps have that feature on them as neither the shampoo or conditioner were locked in. That is the only improvement to this set that I'd suggest.

I checked in the Wayback Machine, and the ingredients for the one I checked (Coconut & Vanilla) were the same at the Native website on January 2, 2019 as they are now.

The confusion is that there are two different versions, one regular and one called "sensitive," for several of the same scents (including Coconut & Vanilla), and they have very different basic ingredient lists. I've verified this at the Native website.

Here's the basic ingredient list for the regular versions. (Some fragrance ingredients are also added for all but the unscented.)

Caprylic/capric triglyceride, tapioca starch, ozokerite, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium hydroxide, Cocos nucifera (coconut) oil, cyclodextrin, Butyrospermium parkii (shea) butter, dextrose (glucose), Lactobacillus acidophilus.

Here's the list for the sensitive versions:

Caprylic/capric triglyceride, arrowroot powder, stearyl alcohol, baking soda, shea butter, coconut oil, hydrogenated castor oil, polyglycerol-3 beeswax, jojoba esters, L. acidophilus, maltodextrin, glyceryl caprylate, glyceryl undecylenate, tocopherol (vitamin E).

I got the regular version of Peony & Jasmine Tea, Sweet Almond & Honey, and Linen & Cotton Flower. Those are sold as women's scents at the Native website, and they are quite sweet and flowery. The peony one is less strong than the other two scent-wise.

They work fine, as these things go, pretty good for deodorizing, not designed to be anti-wet.

They go on fairly dry, not very sticky (make sure you're dry first).

Physical Sunscreens work by sitting on top of the skin to deflect and scatter damaging UV rays away from the skin (whereas chemical sunscreens absorb rays, converts them to heat, then releases). It is one of the most effective sun protectors available, blocking out both short and long UVA rays and all UVB rays. Either type is great, and it depends on what works best with your skin.

I should have read the description on this set better, before ordering as they do not come with a base or top coat which is necessary to get the best longevity out of gel polish.

However I did order the base and top coat from this same brand on Amazon and it works really well. I love the colors in this set and it seems to last about 12-14 days as long as you prep your nails like you should for gel polish.

The color swatch stickers are also nice so you can paint them cure them and apply them to the tops of the bottles and you know which color is which without opening each bottle! Manicures and pedicures are a routine event in our home, especially with restrictions on public outings. With younger children, picking nail polish is a given, so despite the gel’s potential to last for up to two weeks, they manage to remove it in just a few days. For them, though, it means another nail session and new colors, so no big deal. The gel nail polish was hopefully our answer to increase the duration and longevity of their finished nails.

Anzuo Gel Nail Polish offers attractive color kits. We received the Kit 3 set, which contains black, red, white, and three shades of tan to brown. Like others have commented, the lids only contain numbers, and the kit includes stickers where the user has to create the swatches. This is an inconvenience, but not the end of the world. We found it to be a good test to see how the gel polish would actually apply and then finish.

The gel was rather thick, even after keeping it at room temperature, and rolling it to ensure sufficient mixing. With thinner and increased coats, the polish results in deep, beautiful colors that we really enjoy. The white looks like white-out, even with a top clear coat, though. The black and red are the favorites in our home.

The main problem we experienced and shared with others is the inconsistency and deficiencies in the product’s marketing. There are typos, poor translation and grammar, and worse yet, is the inconsistency in the cure times advertised by the company on the Amazon site and the actual shipping box. The box says cure time is 10-30 seconds by LED/UV lamp, but the website says time frames up to 120 seconds. That is a huge difference that seriously impacts the quality and life of the nail finish. We cure using time frames of 60-120 seconds, depending upon the wattage used by our lamp. 1) you need to have a uv/led curing light. You start with the clear base and cure it before applying the gel. Apply the gel and cure, then apply the top coat and cure.

Amore Pacific, based in South Korea, lists "alcohol" as an ingredient in its Color Control Cushion Compact with SPF 50. Since there are good and bad alcohols, I resisted jumping to a negative conclusion especially because I agree with AP regarding the impressive visible benefits conferred by their treatment foundation that has many fans atwitter and aglow.

AP's response to my inquiry was delayed, which I considered either bad (corporate communications) netiquette or bad news. After four workdays, I received a reply thanking me for my "patience" as a response from R&D "to ensure correct information and advice" had not yet been received. When I informed the company that I HAVE no patience and am spoiled by live chats, which provide instant gratification, I received an answer two days later. Apparently, bamboo sap, the primary moisturizing ingredient, is easily contaminated as it's stored for prolonged periods. To prevent "micro-organic pollution," anhydrous alcohol is used. This is ethyl alcohol, which some scientists who write for respected journals warn consumers to avoid because it penetrates the skin barrier and provokes short- and long-term harm, exacerbates oily skin and redness, and may even minimize the efficacy of good ingredients including those that protect against sun damage.

AP is the parent company of Sulwhasoo, which makes a Perfecting Cushion that also includes "alcohol" but not bamboo sap. I don't know what ingredient(s) this brand is protecting.

AP asserts that their anhydrous alcohol is dermatologist approved, but we have no idea who the dermatologist is and whether or not the doctor was paid. AP says that their anhydrous alcohol is patented, but this is just ethyl alcohol with water removed and can't be patented.

The respected Washington, D.C.-based Environmental Working Group (EWG) rates this alcohol a 2 (out of 10) and asserts that anything between 1 and 2 is "low hazard." The overall EWG rating for AP's Color Control Cushion Compact is "4," meaning that it is of *moderate* concern to human health. (The nonprofit group objects most strenuously to the sunscreen octinoxate and to the fragrances included.)

Our U.S. FDA approves the use of ethyl alcohol.

In 2008, the National Institutes of Health urged further investigation, but rigorous double-blind, peer-reviewed studies demand a lot of time and money. Meanwhile, concern lingers. Here's her take on them: They are tricky to apply at first and it takes a while to apply them, so make sure you have something else to keep you busy while you do this. However, once you know what you are doing, they're no longer tricky, but they are still time consuming. It takes time to section out the hair, put the curler in, roll it up, and repeat. Also, it is best if you do this at night if you are someone who has a sensitive head and is prone to headaches from wearing certain hairstyles. However, once I was sitting up, it wasn't long before I felt a tension headache coming on. So, I would say that these are not good for someone who is sensitive to pressure from hairstyles. They don't look heavy, but there is a certain weight to having your hair "pulled" into the curler which can cause discomfort. I decided to sleep with them on, and was able to sleep just fine, since I didn't have any of the curlers directly on the back of my head. Not worth the money These do what they are advertised to do, but results will differ based on a few variables. Remember, the goal is to breathe *through* the mask, not around it. So when there is a better seal, it might be less comfortable to breath.

First, These are memory foam and come vacuum packaged. After you open the bag they take a couple of days to expand to full size. If you use them before they have expanded they will be misshapen and not fit well.

They work best on disposable masks with an adjustable nose wire. The adjustable wire is essential. When you attach the pad centered and directly beneath the nose wire, wear the mask as normal, then squish it onto your face firmly starting in the center of the bridge of your nose and working out. Your ear straps also need to be tighter to maximize the seal all the way around the mask.
Will is stop your glasses fogging completely? no. Is it much much better? yes.
Here is a ranking of performance characteristics.
1. Stability - does a great job of keeping the mask on your nose (assuming a nose wire on the mask).
2. Comfort - significantly reduces abrasion on the bridge of your nose.
3. Seal - this depends on your face, the thickness of the mask, and the strength of the nose wire. I get a pretty good seal and am no longer exhaling directly into my own eyeballs.
4. Reduce glasses fogging - This is directly related to the seal above. It's way better than nothing, but not perfect. I still get a little fog if I breathe hard, but no longer while talking.

Short review: my feet felt better after using this, but the gimmicks get in the way.

Pros:
1. Carry handle works well. It's relatively easy to carry this to and from the sink when full, provided you're okay with the weight.
2. Decent vibration. This is the best part for me, and really the only thing that makes this spa different from a bucket of water.
3. Attachments have a handy storage spot so you don't lose them. That said, I don't care if I lose them because they're useless.

Cons:
1. Useless pedicure attachments. You can't really do anything with the attachments without splashing water everywhere because the sides of the spa are so low. They're also too small to be much use, even if you manage not to splash.
2. Doesn't keep water warm. I really have no idea what they mean by "Thanks to the integrated water heater, the temperature can be maintained or adjusted based on preference" since it doesn't seem to keep the water warm, and you sure can't adjust it any way that I could find.
3. Terrible, pointy rollers. I love foot rollers, but these have tiny, pointy ends that just hurt to use. They're removable, but that just makes them another useless feature.
4. Questionable "soothing red light." It's a light. It's red. There's also no way to turn it off if you'd rather not use it.
5. Loud. It's impossible to watch TV while using this without turning the sound way, way up. If you use it while reading or doing anything else, the motor will drown out most everything - by maybe that's a plus for some people.
6. Other overstated features. The draining outlet isn't an outlet; you just pour the water out the top. "Bubble massage" is just some bubbles in the water. The "cord winder" is just a channel to store the cord underneath. Etc. etc. etc.
7. No info on whether it can be used with bath products, like bubble bath, oils, etc. The product description here does say something about adding bath salts, but it's nowhere in the instructions. Cleaning instructions are to just use vinegar (?), so there's no indication how oils or other products might affect the bath over time.

Overall, my feet did appreciate being soaked in warm water and getting some vibration in the process. But as for all the dubious bells and whistles this spa promises - keep looking. Here IS MY 2 HOURS TO PRETTY CURLS METHOD: Part upper hair at crown of head,  and put hair from the upper head at crown,  in a pony tail for later. Snap the curling system closed, so that there is 2 round circle bands to use to curl with, and put both around head like a double crown head band.
